content: Mineral ascorbates are chemical compounds that consist of salts derived from ascorbic acid, commonly known as vitamin C. These compounds are produced through a specific chemical process. First, ascorbic acid is reacted with mineral carbonates in an aqueous solution. During this reaction, carbon dioxide is released and vented. The resulting reaction product is then dried and subsequently milled into a powder with the desired particle size. The choice of mineral carbonates used in this process can vary and may include calcium carbonate, potassium carbonate, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate, or other mineral forms. These mineral ascorbates are known for their potent antioxidant properties, which make them effective as food preservatives. Additionally, ascorbate salts are often better tolerated by the human body compared to ascorbic acid itself, which is mildly acidic. This improved tolerance can make mineral ascorbates a preferable option for individuals sensitive to the acidity of ascorbic acid.
